subsection.title: Demo Scenario
subsection.description: - Work backward from the Desired Business Impact and approved Essential User Experiences to generate the shortest executable scenario that demonstrates every experience at least once. - Propose the concrete starting state, representative demo input, sequential user actions, and visible expected results instead of asking the user to supply them. - Reuse shared setup and actions when the experiences form one coherent flow. Use separate execution blocks when connecting them would require an unapproved product contract. - For every step, state the user action, visible expected result, and the Essential User Experience it demonstrates. - Show the complete generated scenario, its experience coverage, and how it supports the Desired Business Impact before asking for approval. - End with one overall pass result that requires every Essential User Experience to be observable. - Keep demonstrated claims inside the approved Overview, Solution and Essential User Experiences, and explicit Out of Scope boundary. - Treat a passing demo as evidence that the approved product behavior runs, not as proof of business impact or market validity. - Ask only when the demo exposes a protected product decision about money, permissions, law or regulation, privacy or safety, irreversible data meaning, an external promise, or the acceptance boundary. - Do not omit an Essential User Experience or silently fix a protected product decision.
subsection.example:
**Starting state:** A worker has an upcoming overseas business trip and opens the English practice service.
**Demo input:** `Introduce myself on an overseas business trip`
| Step | User action | Visible expected result | Demonstrates essential experience | |------|-------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------| | 1 | Enters the business-trip introduction topic and starts the conversation | The AI instructor presents the first English question for that situation | Topic-specific practice begins | | 2 | Answers the question in English | A relevant English response and the next question are visible | The conversation adapts to the learner | | 3 | Ends the conversation | The conversation stops and the completed practice state is visible | The learner controls the session |
**Business impact connection:** The worker can rehearse the difficult conversation in a short, controllable session before the trip. The demo shows the product behavior, not whether workplace confidence or trip outcomes improved.
**Overall pass result:** All three Essential User Experiences are observable: topic-specific practice begins, the conversation adapts after the learner answers, and the learner can end the session.
